title: Walkthroughs
audience: For the Principal officer and Logic analyst roles (Harish and Somil hold them): four whole jobs, walked through the screens they will work on.

sections.heading: What the 7 Oct 2026 call asked, and where it is answered

cols: asked or said on the call
rows: Is there access control on the panel: which roles, what access, what permissions
ten fixed roles: two draft and check, one of them sends; Compliance and Ops each change a few things; permissions per action and per screen
The send button must be protected by two factors
a fresh security check to send and at the other protected actions
A few people, or opened up later
two working roles, plus Compliance and Read only; roles are fixed, never user-made
How many people at once; who may change; how many must approve
one open draft per rule set, one author at a time; a second person checks; only the Principal officer sends; Compliance signs Assumptions and Risk scores changes
Is there an approval workflow; should it be stepwise: enter, run, review, send for approval
yes: open, checked, trial run, second check, approved, sent
How often do the values change
Spinach; Somil: an equity return expectation moved from 11 to 10 after four years; Vatsal: funds month on month or quarter on quarter
a review calendar per rule set; M2's registry already reads "annual review" for returns and inflation
When a value changes, what happens to a client who already has a plan
new plans at once; an existing plan at its next refresh, unless pushed now. On the call the answer was: everyone, when it is sent. Vatsal, 8 Oct 2026 replaces it
The plan engine holds central defaults and copies them to each client; a client's numbers hold steady between their reviews
the same aim. Open: where the values live, whether a review reads the central value or the client's copy, and who refreshes the copy
A client sees 19.2 become 18 or 22 and is shocked
net worth today moves with prices; plan numbers move only at a refresh; four update sizes; instalments change as a set or not at all
Rule breaks: a change that takes a client's portfolio outside their risk profile
safety limits a draft must pass (L09); a rule breaks panel in the trial run (L05)
Automatic checks that stop a change ("five errors, cannot proceed"); a lakh of portfolios
a failed check blocks; the trial run is a batch job, sized on the Tech page for 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 plans
Spinach; Vatsal: HoA does the heavy lifting
awkward operating cases: drawn as screen variants and walked through here; maths cases: with the working version owed under W04 and W17
Are versions stored; audit log; version control
sent changes and rule set versions, only ever added; a log line for every change made or refused
Client groups could be 15 to 20, each with its history, why it changed and which portfolios it touched
groups are data; versions are kept per rule set, and each group's history is read from them
An adviser sees, per client, each change and why
L15, which becomes M03's plan versions tab when merged
Versions, history and intelligence per client group are overkill; a simple review and approve will do
what must exist at launch, because it cannot be added afterwards, and what can follow
Keep a saved copy every time anything changes
every refresh writes a saved copy, never edited
Sample plans are affected; they are not a flat file
remade from fixed sample inputs when each sent change goes live
Someone who sat with the app for six months without deciding
a saved first result stays as shown until the person sketches again (V06). On the call the answer was that the numbers will change, and this must be explained
An in-app notice that "we changed this" costs trust; a client who joined a month before a change
Spinach; Vatsal: an email with an explanation, not a notification
house-view changes come on a calendar, inside the client's own review, with the reason; the email (V05)
client views, Ops page; LQ33, LQ21
The hit spreads to sample plans, adviser views and other screens; the life of a change must be mapped
the life of a sent change (below) and a map of what clients read
Access control for the app as well
the app has one kind of user; what each tier unlocks is already on each screen

sections.heading: The design in one place
lines: The rules (Vatsal, 8 Oct 2026):

1. A change is drafted in one rule set. The draft goes: open, checked, trial run done, in second check, approved (or sent back, then open again), sent. Or it is discarded. The second check covers the changes, how it reaches plans and the reason clients read. Changing any of them after approval sends it back.

2. Sending is not applying. A sent change reaches every plan built or refreshed from its go-live time. A plan that already exists stays on its versions until its next refresh. The main board today differs: L06 recalculates every affected client when a change is sent, and Q01 runs on each send. These wireframes draw this way beside it and change nothing on the board. {I04} is described as holding a client's numbers steady between their reviews (7 Oct 2026 call; LQ17, LQ18). In M2's registry, a changed assumption marks the affected plans for recalculation.

3. Only the latest live change of each rule set is used; older ones are records. A refresh reads every rule set's live version when it starts, and never mixes two versions of one. Risk scores are the exception: they are read as of the client's last questionnaire, and the saved copy names that version.
4. A change is pushed now to existing plans only if its sending plan says so. The test, printed on L06: would a prudent adviser phone this client about it today?
5. A plan more than 120 days old refreshes at the next app open (the 120-day limit). A lapsed or cancelled account's plan freezes, and refreshes when the client returns.
6. A change never goes live before it is sent. While a change waits for its set date, its rule set takes no other change, except an urgent hold.

7. Every refresh writes a saved copy. It holds the inputs, the rule set and plan engine versions, each goal's group, the outputs and the actions. It also holds what changed, with a reason on every line (house view, your numbers, your confirmation, time passing, staff edit), the size, and what the client did. Sent changes and saved copies are only added, never edited; a fix is a new record. The record is the stored output, not a promise to recalculate it. On the main board today, L08 reads "the register can reproduce any advice given".

8. The update size decides what the client sees (the update sizes table). Targets are always recalculated. Instalments change as a set or not at all. If any basket's amount moves past the small-change margin, every basket is updated to its target; if none does, nothing changes. A fund on hold or exit updates its own basket. An update still waiting at the next refresh is replaced; the new one shows what changed against the current plan. On the main board, H05 merges waiting updates into one.

9. A fund leaving the approved list goes on hold by default (no new money, units kept). Exit (sell out) is a separate decision, with its own reason. A hold that would empty a basket is blocked until the same draft adds a fund to it. The app never stops a running SIP on its own. It runs until the client accepts the update, and the update says so in plain words.
10. New risk score ranges reach a client only when they next complete or reconfirm the questionnaire.
11. Market readings reach new plans and new investing actions only. Every line has a cushion on either side.

12. Undo is three actions, not a mirror roll-back. Pause: the change stops being the latest, and refreshes use the one before it. Pull back: every update built on it and not yet accepted is replaced by a refresh on the change before it. Clients' own changes are kept, and plan history reads "an update was withdrawn". Fix: a new sent change. Every current plan built on the paused change is refreshed on it at once: first plans, accepted updates, tiny and picture-moved updates alike. A client sees an update only if something moves for them.

13. Two people on every change: the author cannot do the second check, and only the Principal officer sends. One exception: the urgent hold. The Principal officer places it alone, folding draft steps 1 to 8 into one action. It may carry only the basket split it needs to pass the safety limits (L09). Compliance is told at once. A second person signs it off within two working days; until then it stays in force and shows as overdue on L08, L10 and L11 (LQ30).

14. Compliance signs an Assumptions or a Risk scores change before it is sent. An Assumptions change alters the assumption lines and the first result (R08, R09, G01's copy). A Risk scores change alters the risk range a client is told (D09). Compliance is told of every other change when it is sent, and of an urgent hold at once. Most plan screens carry a compliance flag on the main board, so a wider rule would hold up every change (LQ45).

15. Staff use one sign-in for the admin screens and the logic panel: the one decided for M03 on 7 Oct 2026. Roles are fixed; staff cannot make new ones. A greyed-out button is never the real check: the server checks every change. A fresh security check is asked again to send (7 Oct 2026 call), set a date, pause, pull back, place an urgent hold, sign one off, change a role and export.

16. Client groups are data: groupings, a group table, mixes. Funds attach to baskets, not to group table cells. A new range, or a new grouping on a field the app already holds, is data. A grouping that needs a new question needs a new app version.
17. A due review that changes nothing is still recorded: "reviewed, no change", signed by the Principal officer.

18. A draft starts from its rule set's live version. If that version moves while the draft is open (an urgent hold), the draft moves onto it. Its checks and trial run then run again before the second check.

19. A client screen never recalculates a plan number when it opens. It shows the current plan; H05 shows the waiting update. Between refreshes only net worth today moves, with holdings and prices (Gaurav, 7 Oct 2026 call).

20. A house-view change reaches a client on a calendar they were told about: assumptions yearly, live from 1 April; the approved fund list quarterly. It comes inside their own review, with its reason. A change that fails the push test sends no notification; the email explains it (7 Oct 2026 call).

21. Sample plans (R12) and the assumption lines (R08, G01) are remade when a sent change goes live, and dated. A saved first result (X01) records what was shown. It stays, and the nudges keep quoting it, until the person sketches again.

A sent change goes: set for a date, live, replaced (a later change of its rule set is live; plans may still be on it), closed (no active plan is on it). Or it is paused, then fixed. Each step is a log line: who, when, why. At every stage an Adviser or Support can read on L15 which versions a client is on, and why their last update said what it said.

The update size is always decided per client. The table on how changes reach plans lists the sizes each kind can produce. A push refreshes every plan it picks, but messages a client only for a to-accept or urgent update.

A hold resets the basket's remaining split to 100 for new money (largest remainder, whole numbers). It then checks the safety limits (L09) before it is placed. If a limit breaks, the hold screen says so and asks for a split.

Each pushed change has a batch plan (LQ14). An urgent hold or a fix goes to everyone at once. A routine hold goes to 200 clients an hour, 10:00 to 18:00 IST. An exit goes in even daily batches over five working days.

Small-change margin: per basket, the larger of Rs 1,000 or 10 percent of the running amount; for a goal's funded share, 5 points. Amounts are whole hundreds, and a basket's funds add up to its amount (largest remainder). For a client not investing through the app, each basket's new target is compared with the last target shown.

Second reasons: a fund entering or leaving the client's split also names the Funds change that altered the basket. A risk range changed at a questionnaire reads your confirmation; it also names the Risk scores change if the same score read differently before.

Why four sizes: under the M4 reconciliation rule, most plans invest the whole surplus. So a change in returns or inflation leaves instalments as they are, and moves how far they are expected to go. In a rough run, an assumptions change is tiny for about 33 plans in 100, picture moved for about 54 and to accept for about 13. Picture moved asks for nothing, so it is not chased.

The email (7 Oct 2026 call): one per sent house-view change that alters what clients see. It says what changed, why, and that the plan takes it up at the client's next review, with the date. Its wording is to come, kept with the other message wording. When it goes out: LQ33.

Calls made while building (logic plan, 8 Oct 2026), open to veto: Compliance signs only Assumptions and Risk scores changes; a fresh security check at every other protected action; what moves on client screens, and when; the steps of a draft, and what each records; the stages of a sent change.

lines: What the client saw:

- Client C11: the wrong mix at the review of 6 Dec 2027, equity from 65 to 56 percent of the mix; accepted, the SIPs changed on 8 Dec. On 17 Dec, an update with a step that undoes the cut in equity, accepted 18 Dec.

- Client C12: the review of 15 Dec 2027, not accepted. At 11:40 on 16 Dec the update was pulled back: the plan refreshed on version co-2 as a tiny update (V04). A tiny update again at the review of 12 Mar 2028.
- No email: none was proposed for REL08. How the fix is explained to clients is open (LQ23).
- Per 1,000 clients, about 14 plans were built on version co-3 in its 16 days, plus the first plans built in those days.
What was stored:

- Change REL08 (version co-3): mix MP6 at 0/24/10/10/56/0, with the typed reason for its warning. Drafted by Logic analyst 01, approved and sent by Principal officer 01; live 16:00 on 30 Nov 2027. The approval records that the example clients panel was not opened.

- Change REL09 (version co-4): the fix, mix MP6 at 0/15/10/8/67/0. Drafted by Logic analyst 01, approved and sent by Principal officer 01; live 12:00 on 17 Dec 2027.
- The saved copies: C11 on co-3 (6 Dec, accepted) and co-4 (17 Dec, accepted 18 Dec); C12 on co-3 (15 Dec, not accepted) and co-2 (16 Dec, tiny).
- The incident entry of 17 Dec 2027, by Compliance 01 (LQ23).
What could have stopped it (each line is open):
- to be decided: whether approval waits until the checker has opened every trial run panel (LQ22). The example clients panel showed equity down 9 points and was not opened.
- to be decided: a hard limit on how far one investment type can move (LQ22). The big-jump warning caught the 9-point move on two types, and a typed reason let it through.
